story: At 8:17 on a sunny Tuesday evening in Sumter Oaks, Gary heads down Magnolia Loop toward his own house, moving at an easy, patient pace. Over at Rosa's House, Donna is brimming with enthusiasm as she pitches Rosa a pumpkin patch plan built around clip-on lights, a fabric banner, and a hay-bale skirt that tucks on so nothing counts as permanent, and she wants it ready for Hal tomorrow. Hal, back at Town Hall, is determined to get written notices filed on Gary's cart modifications and Donna's flamingo count before the 9 AM committee meeting, while Rosa, content as ever, is checking her per-diem shifts to find free evenings for building the parade cart.
events: Hal (architectural review desk): File written notices on Gary's cart modifications (L-01) and Donna's flamingo count (L-02) ahead of tomorrow's 9 AM committee meeting
Rosa (rosa shift schedule): Check my per-diem shifts to find free evenings this week for building the parade cart

gary.thought_process: I read the bulletin board last tick, so no need to stare at it again. It's 8:17 PM on a Tuesday, the parade is Saturday, and my Architectural Review application is still pending. Rosa offered to walk the sketches over with me, and I've already offered them to the desk once. Nobody's around to talk to. The sensible thing is to go to town square and check in on the application, or at least to prep. Actually, I've checked everything twice already. A quiet walk home to double-check the clamp list one more time and tinker feels right, and it keeps me from rushing past the law. Home it is, where my cart and tools are.

parameters.content: Heading home to go over the wiring sketches and clamp list once more while I wait on Review approval.

donna.thought_process: Rosa and I have been sketching at her dining table for a few ticks and she just proposed a pumpkin-patch theme with clip-on lights and a removable banner. Everything stays removable, so it should clear Architectural Review under L-01, and it fits the Halloween parade on the 31st. I shouldn't keep re-asking her anything. I should react to her idea, add something concrete, and keep the sketching moving. Then once we have a design, I can pull Gary into the plan and still get to the pickleball practice.

parameters.content: Rosa, I love the pumpkin patch! Let's do the clip-on lights and the fabric banner, and I'll add a little hay-bale skirt along the bottom that just tucks on, so nothing's permanent and Review can't say a word. Pencil that in and let's get it to Hal tomorrow.

hal.thought_process: I'm at Town Hall with the bulletin board schedule fresh in mind and the committee meeting at nine tomorrow. Nobody is around, so the proper channel is the paperwork. The architectural review desk is where my complaints about Gary's cart modifications (L-01) and Donna's flamingo count (L-02) belong, on record and by the book. Two scraps of gossip on the street won't settle anything, but a filed notice will. Fair is fair, though: I'll stick to what I've actually counted and seen from the street.

parameters.content: File written notices on Gary's cart modifications (L-01) and Donna's flamingo count (L-02) ahead of tomorrow's 9 AM committee meeting

rosa.thought_process: Donna and I have the first design down: removable pumpkin garland and a clip-on bat banner, all Review-friendly under L-01. The dinner worked, everyone's at the table, and the cart plan is moving. It's already past 8 PM and I have to think about my shift schedule this week. Since Donna and I have been sketching side by side for a few ticks, I shouldn't keep repeating the same sketch action. Better to check my per-diem schedule so I know when I can be free to help build and decorate before Saturday's parade.

parameters.content: Check my per-diem shifts to find free evenings this week for building the parade cart

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
